title: regional gpu capacity checkin 2026-03-11
body:
Meeting: Infrastructure weekly capacity check-in (informal notes)
Date: 2026-03-11
Attendees: Eliot Rivera (chair), Maya Chen, Sanjay Patel, Lina Romero, on-call SRE (rotation: week A)
Duration: 40m

Summary:
- Short sync focused on regional GPU headroom, recent surge that hit us last Friday, and a quick playbook rehearsal for multi-region failover.
- Primary requests: confirm where to trigger cross-region bursting, finalize buffer policy for Dedicated pools, and land autoscaler tuning for small-model heavy workloads.

1) Current cluster snapshot (end of day 2026-03-10):
- us-west-2: 680 GPUs total (NVIDIA H100 equivalent nodes). Average util last 24h: 72% overall, tail peak 94% (short spikes between 14:00-15:00 PDT).
- us-east-1: 540 GPUs. Avg util 61%, tail peak 80%. One node group undergoing driver upgrade (in progress, 36/120 instances updated).
- eu-west-1: 420 GPUs. Avg util 52%, steady.
- ap-southeast-1: 180 GPUs. Avg util 49%, but reported higher p99 latencies for embeddings route (see incident notes).
- Buffer policy: current soft buffer target = 12% free GPUs by region. Observed underprovisioning in us-west-2 during Friday surge where effective free capacity briefly hit 4%.

2) Incident recap (Fri 2026-03-06 surge):
- What happened: sudden burst of requests from two mid-market customers running heavy chat workloads (~50k tokens/min each) + one internal stress test. Autoscaler reacted but scale up lag + placement fragmentation led to queuing and model fallbacks triggering (we downgraded some requests to smaller quantized variants).
- Impact: 11% increase in tail latency for hosted-api customers routed to us-west-2 for ~18 minutes. No SLA breach for Dedicated customers (they are pinned to reserved pools).
- Mitigation that worked: cross-region reroute to us-east-1 policy kicked in after 7m; automated model fallback reduced cost but increased error rate for a subset of calls.
- Follow-up: implement faster warm-up for cold VM families (pre-provision a tiny extra pool), reduce autoscaler evaluation window from 120s -> 60s for chat-heavy routes.

3) Regional action items (owner + ETA):
- us-west-2: add temporary 64-GPU burst pool (spot/reserved mix) and enable pre-warm script for 2 most common node types. Owner: Maya Chen, ETA: 2026-03-15.
- us-east-1: finish driver/AMI rollout (remaining 84 instances). Owner: Sanjay Patel, ETA: 2026-03-13. Rollout note: use canary 8-instance group, validate KV cache persistence.
- eu-west-1: no action; monitor for registration failures after recent kubelet change. Owner: Lina Romero, ETA: 2026-03-18.
- ap-southeast-1: investigate embeddings p99 latency increase; suspected noisy neighbor from one customer. Owner: on-call SRE, ETA: 2026-03-12 (follow-up in separate incident doc).

4) Autoscaler and routing changes proposed:
- Autoscaler tuning: decrease scale-up cool-down from 180s to 90s for routes tagged chat-heavy. Increase per-node placement packing to favor larger instances for long-lived chat sessions.
- Routing: tighten cross-region reroute threshold from 90th percentile latency > 350ms to > 300ms for critical customers (customer-tiers: enterprise).
- Policy: add a transient-burst allowance (10% extra capacity, reclaimed after 30m) for Dedicated customers in case of regional hot spots.

5) Surge-playbook rehearsal notes (we ran a short tabletop):
- Trigger criteria we practiced on: sustained queue length growth > 120s + p95 token latency > 400ms for 3 consecutive evaluation windows.
- Primary steps: a) increase pre-warm count b) reroute non-enterprise to fallback region c) enable model-quantize fallback for non-critical routes d) notify CS for impacted customers.
- Gaps found: playbook lacked a clear owner for Slack broadcast in first 5 minutes. Proposed: rotate this responsibility to the on-call SRE + add a small pre-written template.

6) Capacity planning notes (Q2 outlook):
- Forecast: expected 18% demand growth in hosted-api chat and 12% for embeddings across Q2. Planned procurement: two additional H100-equivalent node pools (us-west-2 and eu-west-1) to arrive mid-April.
- Cost tradeoff: spot vs reserved mix analysis shows 22% expected saving with 60% spot for non-Dedicated workloads, but increases preemption risk. Proposal: 50/50 spot/reserved for new pools and evaluate after 6 weeks.

7) Open questions / blockers:
- Can platform-ops approve a one-time quota bump in us-west-2 for March 13-20 to support customer migrations? (raised to Finance & Ops).
- Do we want to automate warm pre-provisioning when forecast signals exceed 80% predicted util for next 6 hours? (requires a forecast-to-provision pipeline; infra effort ≈ 3 wk).

8) Action item recap (short):
- Maya: create pre-warm orchestration playbook + PR for burst pool (ETA 03/15).
- Sanjay: complete AMI rollout and open post-rollout verification ticket (ETA 03/13).
- Lina: monitor eu-west kubelet change + report (ETA 03/18).
- On-call SRE: investigate ap-southeast latency (ETA 03/12).
- Eliot: draft Slack broadcast template and update surge-playbook doc (ETA 03/13).

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a lightweight regional "warm cache" service that keeps small VMs registered and cached for fastest cold-start path (prototype 1-week spike).
- Add a runtime metric that marks "placement fragmentation" (count of free GPUs that cannot satisfy largest pending request by memory). This would help automations decide to trigger cross-region bursting earlier.

References / links:
- Regional capacity plan (confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/123456789/Regional+Capacity+Plan
- Related Jira: INF-4782 (autoscaler tuning), INF-4810 (us-west burst pool), INF-4821 (ap-southeast embeddings latency)

Next sync: 2026-03-18 (same time).

Unresolved: need final sign-off from finance for temporary quota bump, and product to confirm that non-enterprise fallback to quantized models is acceptable for the next 2 planned rehearsals.

Informal notes style: keep iterating here — this doc is a working log, not the final runbook.
